domain_title: Energy Sovereignty and the People’s Energy Dividend
research_domain_title: Energy Sovereignty, Public Energy Returns, and National Energy Prosperity
note: Major national doctrine. Preserves private innovation while establishing durable public return from strategic energy resources, rights-of-way, publicly supported research, federal waters, mineral access, export permits, and nationally significant infrastructure. Allocation percentages are illustrative design parameters requiring modeling — not locked law. Architecture only; legal drafting and fund modeling remain 0%. Sourced EIA/DOE structural baselines registered separately; architecture ≠ evidence of current public-return institutions.

governing_principle.text: The nation should produce enough reliable, affordable energy to meet its own essential needs, protect itself from foreign coercion, strengthen every community, and export genuine surplus energy so that part of the resulting wealth flows permanently into public and community ownership.

memorable_principle.text: Power America first. Strengthen the free world second. Return the profit to the people.

doctrine_statement.text: Energy is both an essential public foundation and a strategic national asset. The republic shall maintain sufficient diverse domestic capacity to protect every household, community, industry, and defense need from foreign coercion. Genuine surplus energy may be exported, but the people must receive a permanent financial return from the resources, infrastructure, legal protections, and accumulated knowledge that make those exports possible.

priority_sequence.principle: Serve the people first. Strengthen the nation second. Export the surplus third.
priority_sequence.export_constraint: Exports should never be allowed to create domestic scarcity, destabilize household bills, or force taxpayers to subsidize infrastructure built primarily for foreign sales.

sovereignty_not_autarky.summary: Energy independence does not mean isolation or that America never imports a barrel, mineral, component, or electron. Trade can improve efficiency and resilience.
sovereignty_not_autarky.definition: America possesses enough diverse domestic production, reserves, manufacturing, transmission, and technical capacity that no foreign power can seriously threaten its essential energy supply or dictate its national policy.

diversified_system.summary: National independence must not depend on one fuel. Not an ideological contest between fossil fuels and renewable energy — an engineering question.
diversified_system.engineering_question: Which combination provides the greatest reliability, lowest full cost, smallest long-term burden, strongest domestic supply chain, and greatest public benefit?
develop: oil and natural gas during a managed transition
biomass and renewable natural gas where sustainable
future hydrogen or synthetic fuels where economically proven

sourced_context_baselines.note: Descriptive EIA/DOE facts supporting that the U.S. already has substantial production and export capacity. These do not prove that current exports create public prosperity or that the proposed institutions exist.

items.text: In 2024 the United States produced more primary energy than it consumed and recorded the highest net energy exports in EIA records dating to 1949.
U.S. electricity net generation reached a record 4.43 thousand terawatthours in 2025 per EIA.
U.S. crude-oil production reached a record 13.6 million barrels per day in 2025 per EIA.
U.S. LNG exports reached approximately 5.5 trillion cubic feet in 2025 per DOE Natural Gas Imports and Exports Monthly year-to-date totals.
Even as a net petroleum exporter, the United States continues importing some crude oil and petroleum products for refinery and market needs (EIA Energy Explained).

american_energy_and_resilience_corporati.name: American Energy and Resilience Corporation
american_energy_and_resilience_corporati.summary: Constitutionally chartered public institution holding the people’s financial interest in nationally significant energy assets — not a nationalization of the whole energy industry.
may: invest alongside private companies in export terminals, transmission, storage, nuclear generation, and strategic infrastructure
hold royalties and public equity interests
purchase or develop public generation where markets fail
collect public returns from export activity
invest profits through a sovereign public wealth fund
american_energy_and_resilience_corporati.does_not: Control every power plant or fuel producer. Ensures public ownership and revenue where public assets, guarantees, land, research, financing, or national market access materially enable the enterprise.

national_energy_prosperity_fund.summary: Permanent sovereign wealth fund. Principal generally remains invested; only a disciplined portion of annual earnings is spent. Energy becomes a public fundraising mechanism without turning extraction into a short-term political spending spree.
revenue_sources: public patents and publicly financed energy technology
profits from publicly owned energy assets

illustrative_distributable_allocation.note: Percentages are not locked law and must be modeled before any statute claim.

debt_first_then_prosperity.summary: During the debt-reduction era, a larger share of export profits prioritizes solvency and strategic capacity; as debt and interest burdens decline, allocation automatically shifts toward local ownership and human prosperity.
debt_first_then_prosperity.public_promise: We will use energy abundance first to restore national solvency, and then convert that abundance into permanent local ownership and human prosperity.

community_energy_dividends.summary: Communities producing or hosting energy infrastructure should receive direct benefits. A community should never provide land, water, roads, labor, environmental capacity, and social consent while seeing almost all the wealth leave.
community_energy_dividends.links_to_resource_sovereignty: Aligns with Community Resource Compacts and Community Resource Dividends.

export_forms.summary: Energy exports are not only crude oil or LNG. Long-term national wealth is greater if America also exports equipment, technology, engineering, and ownership behind global energy systems.
forms: nuclear fuel and reactor technology under strict safeguards

domestic_prosperity_test.summary: Every major export expansion should undergo a Domestic Prosperity Test. Exports should be conditioned on affordable domestic service, not treated as an unlimited right.
questions: Will it raise household energy prices?
Will it consume grid or pipeline capacity needed domestically?
Who pays for the infrastructure?
What public return is received?
What communities bear the burden?
Does it strengthen or weaken industrial competitiveness?
What happens during an emergency?
Can exports be temporarily reduced to protect essential domestic supply?
Does the project leave permanent public wealth?
Are environmental and closure costs fully funded?

strategic_export_agreements.summary: Energy exports should support foreign policy without dependence on unstable authoritarian buyers — just as the nation should not depend on authoritarian suppliers.
prioritize: countries reducing dependence on hostile suppliers

community_owned_stack.summary: National sovereignty begins locally. Local systems remain connected to state and national grids while reducing household exposure to price shocks and keeping more energy spending inside the community.

guardrails.summary: Energy revenue must not become a hidden budget politicians raid before elections. No elected official should direct energy-fund investments toward donors or favored companies.

environmental_responsibility.summary: Energy independence cannot mean transferring irreversible damage to rural communities. Abundance with stewardship.

energy_sovereignty_test.purpose: Screen energy production, export, fund, and community-return proposals.
questions: Does the design serve households and communities before export surplus?
Is capacity diverse enough that no foreign power can coerce essential supply or national policy?
Does the people receive a durable return from public assets, rights-of-way, research, or nationally significant infrastructure that enable the enterprise?
Would the American Energy and Resilience Corporation hold public interest without nationalizing the whole industry?
Are Prosperity Fund allocations disciplined, with principal protected and spending formulas resistant to election-year raids?
Does debt-era allocation prioritize solvency before shifting to local ownership and dividends?
Do hosting communities receive equity, bill relief, restoration, and closure funding — not only externalized burdens?
Does every major export pass the Domestic Prosperity Test?
Are environmental and decommissioning costs fully funded?
Is private innovation preserved while public return is secured?
